UnitStatement: Repo-native skills are reusable method packs that a bounded Type 2 agent may load at runtime.
Skills are not agents and do not have their own decision rights, write scopes, or interaction surfaces.
A skill method bundle states the task shape it supports.
A skill method bundle states which tools are preferred or allowed.
A skill method bundle states which runtime overrides matter.
A skill method bundle states what outputs should exist.
A skill method bundle states how to QA the run.
AGENT_TASK.md is the canonical loader for repo-native skills.
SKILLMAKER owns skill design, contract evolution, and subsystem governance.
Skill outcomes must conform to HELPS_HUMANS R10, HELPS_HUMANS R12, and the Design Outcomes for Skill Contracts section.
A new skill is appropriate when the role stays the same but the method and toolchain vary.
A new skill is appropriate when write authority is supplied by the bounded TASK brief and the interaction model stays the same.
A bounded task should not become a new agent merely because it has a different tool recipe.
When TASK loads a skill, human instructions in the run brief have highest precedence.
The TASK shell hard authorization boundary takes precedence over the skill contract.
Skill defaults have lower precedence than the skill contract.
A skill must never widen write authority beyond the TASK shell and effective bounded task brief.
When a persona agent dispatches TASK with TaskSkill, TASK automatically loads the skill's SKILL.md and companion files.
Skill hydration guarantees the worker receives the full contract without the orchestrator reconstructing it in the dispatch prompt.
SKILL.md is the authoritative method and output contract for a skill.
BRIEF_SCHEMA.md defines the dispatch contract for invoking a skill through TASK.
TOOL_POLICY.md defines the tool allowlist and preferences for a skill.
QA_CHECKS.md defines output validity checks for a skill.
RuntimeOverrides supply runtime parameters, and CustomInstructions supply run-specific reinforcement.
CustomInstructions do not replace the skill contract.
Each skill must live in its own folder under skills/<skill_name>/.
Each skill folder must include SKILL.md, BRIEF_SCHEMA.md, TOOL_POLICY.md, and QA_CHECKS.md.
Skill folders may include optional extras such as examples, notes, and helper templates for humans.
Every SKILL.md should include YAML frontmatter with at least name and description.
Every SKILL.md should state the skill purpose and suitable task shapes.
Every SKILL.md should state required inputs and optional runtime overrides.
Every SKILL.md should state output expectations, TASK safety, and important non-negotiable constraints.
The frontmatter is the portable discovery surface for a skill.
The Markdown body is the Chirality execution guidance for a skill.
BRIEF_SCHEMA.md, TOOL_POLICY.md, and QA_CHECKS.md are required Chirality-specific companion files layered on the core skill contract.
Skills may reference deterministic tools under tools/ by policy, not by hidden assumption.
Good skill design makes preferred tools explicit.
Good skill design makes disallowed tools explicit.
Good skill design states when to fall back from tools to manual or LLM reasoning.
Briefs and skills are orthogonal.
A task brief provides run-specific authority, scope inputs, write permissions, overrides, and expected outputs.
A skill provides the method pack for a recurring task shape.
The metadata.chirality-task-profile frontmatter field should normally be NONE.
Non-NONE metadata.chirality-task-profile values are deprecated compatibility metadata, not write-scope grants.
deliverable-consistency should normally begin with tools/validation/scan_deliverable_consistency.py, then read only flagged files and nearby context.
PDF2MD dispatches TASK + pdf2md-page for text transcription.
When PDF2MD uses ASSET_MODE=prose, it dispatches TASK + pdf2md-page-assets for page-bounded figure, table, and image discovery.
PDF2MD deterministic tools materialize crops and CSVs, anchor page Markdown, aggregate the public asset manifest, and validate references.
DBM_PUBLISHER first runs deterministic section mapping and section context packet generation.
DBM_PUBLISHER dispatches TASK + dbm-section-publish once per approved publication section with its read-only context packet.
DBM_PUBLISHER dispatches TASK + dbm-publish for package assembly, knowledge coverage and open-items records, and content adequacy.
After DBM package assembly, TASK + dbm-postauthor-concordance builds a post-authoring evidence bundle for human disposition.
TASK + dbm-concordance-verify may provide optional semantic cross-section consistency observations.
DBM publication skills remain publication-local and should be confined to _Publication/DBM/ scopes rather than mutating KTY-local truth.
WORKING_ITEMS dispatches TASK + dbm-draft-review to review a human-prepared draft DBM against the governed knowledge base.
dbm-draft-review runs scan_section_coverage.py, extract_claims.py, scan_tbd_markers.py, and check_body_thinness.py as deterministic substrate tools.
dbm-draft-review uses agent judgment to compare substrate against governed truth and prepare candidate findings.
The human dispositions dbm-draft-review findings through the REVIEW agent.
dbm-concordance-seed is legacy and is no longer dispatched by DBM_PUBLISHER.
Concordance has moved from the pre-authoring gate to post-authoring evidence bundle review.
Agents must treat skills/ as a live skill root rather than relying on hard-coded skill lists in narrative documents.
Each immediate subfolder of skills/ that contains SKILL.md is a repo-native skill.
Agent guidance says to read skills/README.md first for the shared contract.
When a specific skill is requested, the agent should inspect SKILL.md, BRIEF_SCHEMA.md, TOOL_POLICY.md, and QA_CHECKS.md in that skill folder.
Agents should use the live skills/ folder rule for skill counts and use AGENTS.md plus tools/REGISTRY.md for indexes.
Agents should not assume another document's embedded skill list is current.
If live folder contents and a canonical index disagree, agents must surface the discrepancy explicitly.
A well-bounded and auditable TASK run with a skill, scope, and tool permissions should probably be a skill rather than a new top-level agent.
For new skills, the TaskSkill token should match the skill folder and name frontmatter exactly.
New skill names should prefer lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens only.
After adding or renaming skills, run tools/validation/validate_skill_metadata.py on skills.
validate_skill_metadata.py scans every immediate skill folder under skills/.
validate_skill_metadata.py validates both the basic authoring contract and the machine-consumed runtime contract.
The basic authoring contract includes name, description, folder alignment, and required TOOL_POLICY.md presence.
The machine-consumed runtime contract includes metadata.chirality-* values, canonical allowed-tools syntax, and tool-path resolution under tools/.
The skill template is used when creating a new repo-native skill under skills/.
Skill contracts conform to AGENT_HELPS_HUMANS design outcomes for skill contracts and compliance requirements R10 plus R12.
AGENT_SKILLMAKER owns skill contract evolution and subsystem governance.
New skills must pass tools/validation/validate_skill_metadata.py.
The skill template frontmatter includes name, description, optional compatibility, optional allowed-tools, and chirality metadata.
The skill template sets metadata.chirality-skill-version to "1" and metadata.chirality-task-profile to NONE.
A skill Purpose section states the recurring bounded task the skill supports.
A skill Suitable agent shells section lists TASK and any optional brief-shape constraints.
A skill Inputs section distinguishes required and optional fields.
A skill Runtime overrides section records each key's meaning, default, and allowed values.
A skill Tool usage section lists preferred tools and optional tools when applicable.
A skill Tool usage section lists disallowed tools.
A skill Outputs section lists expected artifacts.
A skill Non-negotiable constraints section records constraints.
A skill QA expectations section records checks.
Every skill must include BRIEF_SCHEMA.md.
BRIEF_SCHEMA.md documents the dispatch contract for invoking the skill through TASK.
BRIEF_SCHEMA.md must document required brief fields, optional fields, RuntimeOverrides guidance, and recommended CustomInstructions content.
CustomInstructions in a brief carry run-specific reinforcement and do not replace SKILL.md.
Every skill must include TOOL_POLICY.md.
Implicit tool assumptions are a design defect.
TOOL_POLICY.md uses canonical section headings for Preferred tool order, Allowed deterministic tools, Expected use of reasoning, Disallowed use, and Write boundary.
The Allowed deterministic tools section uses TASK-enforced and Operationally invoked H3 subsections.
Every TOOL_POLICY.md must include Allowed deterministic tools, Disallowed use, and Write boundary.
Preferred tool order and Expected use of reasoning may be skipped when no content applies.
Every skill must include QA_CHECKS.md.
QA_CHECKS.md documents minimum output validity checks, failure reporting expectations, and required evidence or logs.
The allowed-tools frontmatter field is machine-consumed by TASK during skill resolution.
allowed-tools must be a comma-space-delimited list of command specs.
Each allowed-tools command spec has the form <interpreter> <repo-relative-tool-path>:<scope_glob>.
allowed-tools specs cannot include flags, extra arguments, or commas inside a spec.
The interpreter token in an allowed-tools spec is a single token such as python3.
The repo-relative-tool-path token in an allowed-tools spec is a single token relative to repo root.
The scope_glob follows the final colon in an allowed-tools command spec.
If allowed-tools is malformed, TASK rejects the skill with an error.
The allowed-tools field should be omitted entirely when a skill has no deterministic tool requirements.
A skill folder name should be the TaskSkill token used in briefs.
The name frontmatter should match the skill folder name.
Skill folder names should prefer lowercase ASCII letters, digits, and hyphens.
After creating or updating a skill, run python3 tools/validation/validate_skill_metadata.py skills.
validate_skill_metadata.py checks all skill folders under skills and does not target one named skill unless given a narrower root.
